Claude Joins Wall Street
Anthropic makes its
Nasdaq debut
today under the ticker ANT, after pricing its shares at $83 apiece yesterday, above the company’s expected range of $70-$78 per share. The AI company raised $68.5B at a $1.5T valuation, making it the second-largest initial public offering after Elon Musk’s SpaceX, which raised roughly $86B at a $1.8T valuation.
Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI employees, Anthropic differentiated itself as a safety-first AI company. CEO Dario Amodei has advocated for
industry guardrails
against cyberattacks, weapons development, and rogue AI agents
while touting AI's potential to
cure diseases
and accelerate economic growth. Claude's popularity increased this year after being blacklisted by the Pentagon over its military restrictions; the standoff briefly pushed Claude ahead of OpenAI's ChatGPT in downloads. Compare the leading labs on philosophy and performance
here
The decision to go public was largely driven by soaring computing costs, with nearly $900B in spending commitments through 2045. See how the IPO could
affect your investment portfolio
GTA VI Arrives
Grand Theft Auto VI
hit gaming consoles
at midnight local time today, kicking off a rolling global launch that has been 13 years in the making. Rockstar Games’ latest flagship installment has already generated over $1.6B with 17 million preorders; see its
cultural impact in charts
The open-world sequel features 600,000 animations and GTA’s first nonoptional female protagonist, Lucia, voiced by actress Manni L. Perez. GTA VI’s release caps a wait so long it
spawned a meme
about major historical events preceding the game’s arrival. Paid-time-off requests for launch day
jumped nearly 13%
compared with equivalent dates in 2024 and 2025, and roughly one in five salaried workers plan to take the day off to play.
Analysts estimate the game could bring in $3B to $5B in its first week alone. Video games generated $184.5B in 2022, exceeding the combination of box office revenue ($26B) and music releases ($26.2B), a trend that has continued post-COVID-19. Panic at the Costco
US customers have been
bulk purchasing pantry staples
and generators at Costco, investment firm Mizuho Securities reported this week. Mizuho raised its target stock price for the company from $1,100 to $1,150 amid the trend, which the firm says began in late October.
Much of the purchasing, known colloquially as panic buying, is linked to social media rumors
of a blackout
that has not materialized to date. Nonetheless, recent
tech outages
—including Microsoft, Apple, Chase, United, and the Federal Aviation Administration—have exacerbated some Americans’ concerns that US infrastructure is vulnerable to cyberattacks. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and other US officials have
publicly dispelled
allegations that the recent outages are related.
Costco has nonetheless reported a jump in purchases of staples, including rice, canned goods, water, paper products, batteries, and generators. Mizuho expects Walmart, Sam’s Club, Home Depot, and Lowe’s may also see revenue growth.
